chunks: Bear yourself towards your brother in such a way that if he disregards kinship you keep to it; when he turns away be kind to him and draw near to him; when he withholds spend for him; when he goes away approach him; when he is harsh be lenient; when he commits wrong think of (his) excuse for it, so much so as though you are a slave of him and he is the benevolent master over you.

key_terms.جُمُودِهِ: his withholding or stagnation in giving
key_terms.صَرْمِ: disregarding or cutting off kinship ties

ai.seo_question: How should one behave towards a brother who is distant or harsh according to Shia ethics?
ai.summary: Delivered to Imam Hasan (peace be upon him) as he departed for the Battle of Siffin, this instruction from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) serves as a strategic blueprint for maintaining social cohesion amidst political turmoil. It emphasizes proactive, unilateral effort in preserving kinship (silat al-rahib) by adopting a posture of humility and gratitude, effectively neutralizing the other party's potential hostility or distance. This approach reflects the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and *hilm* (forbearance) as active virtues that sustain community bonds even when reciprocity is not immediately evident.
